context.analysis:
## Overview
• Cloud-native, Amazon-style online bookstore offering physical and electronic books, reviews, and recommendations.
• Designed to scale globally while ensuring high availability, strict security, and GDPR/CCPA compliance.

## Key Elements
• Customer (Shopper)
• Registered Reviewer / Community Member
• Store Administrator / Content Moderator
• Online Bookstore Software System
• Payment Gateway (Stripe/PayPal)
• Shipping Provider APIs (FedEx/UPS)
• Identity & Notification Service (AWS SES)

## Relationships
• Users -> Online Bookstore: HTTPS (TLS 1.3)
• Online Bookstore -> Payment Gateway: HTTPS/REST with mTLS
• Online Bookstore -> Shipping Provider APIs: HTTPS/REST via AWS SQS async queuing
• Online Bookstore -> Identity & Notification Service: HTTPS/SMTP
• Containers -> Containers: mTLS and SPIFFE/SPIRE via AWS App Mesh

## Technology Stack
• AWS Cloud (us-east-1, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1): Multi-region deployment for global performance.
• Amazon Route 53: Latency-based routing for sub-2s page loads.
• AWS ECS/EKS: Independent container architecture for checkout, catalog, and reviews.
• AWS Secrets Manager & KMS: Secure credential injection and PII encryption at rest.
• AWS X-Ray & CloudWatch: Centralized observability, tracing, and autoscaling.

## Rationale
• Decoupled micro-containers and multi-region AWS routing ensure 99.95% uptime and scalability for 1M MAU.
• Strict adherence to TLS 1.3, mTLS, AWS KMS encryption, and audit logging guarantees GDPR/CCPA and OWASP compliance.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
[An Amazon-style e-commerce site providing physical and electronic book sales, personalized recommendations, and reviews. Built to handle 1M MAU across global regions with strict GDPR/CCPA compliance.]

## Key Elements
* **Users:** Customer (Shopper), Reviewer, Store Administrator
* **Frontend:** Single Page Application (React / TypeScript) via Amazon S3 and Amazon CloudFront
* **Edge/Routing:** Amazon API Gateway / Application Load Balancer
* **Core Services (AWS ECS / Fargate):** Catalogue & Search Service, Checkout & Cart Service, Recommendation Service, Review Service
* **Data & Caching:** Amazon RDS (PostgreSQL with read replicas), Amazon ElastiCache (Redis), Amazon OpenSearch
* **Messaging & Streaming:** Amazon SQS / SNS (with DLQ), Amazon Kinesis
* **External Systems:** Payment Gateway, Shipping Provider APIs, Identity & Notification Service

## Relationships
* **SPA to API Gateway:** HTTPS / JSON
* **API Gateway to Core Services:** HTTPS / REST
* **Service-to-Service:** gRPC with mTLS via AWS App Mesh / Envoy sidecars
* **Streaming:** Event capture via Amazon Kinesis, feeding the Recommendation Service
* **Asynchronous Messaging:** Transactional Outbox Pattern to Amazon SQS for shipping and payment APIs

## Technology Stack
* **Cloud Infrastructure:** AWS (us-east-1, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1) for global multi-region presence
* **Compute:** Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate for operational simplicity and container orchestration
* **Database & Search:** Amazon RDS PostgreSQL (with regional data residency) and Amazon OpenSearch for R-01 catalogue search
* **Caching:** Amazon ElastiCache (Redis) for sub-50ms recommendation lookups
* **Observability & Security:** OpenTelemetry, AWS CloudWatch, AWS Secrets Manager, and AWS KMS for encryption with CMKs

## Rationale
[AWS Fargate combined with Amazon CloudFront and ElastiCache ensures sub-2-second page loads globally while scaling dynamically to 1M MAU. Regional database endpoints, PII masking, and outbox patterns enforce GDPR/CCPA compliance and 99.95% availability.]

Single Page Application (SPA).analysis:
## Overview
An Amazon-style online bookstore providing catalog browsing, secure checkout, reviews, and recommendations. The frontend is a scalable Single Page Application deployed globally on AWS.

## Key Elements
- Single Page Application (SPA) (React, TypeScript)
- Routing & Shell Component (React Router)
- Catalog & Search Module
- Cart & Checkout State Machine (Redux Toolkit)
- Recommendation & Review Widgets
- API Client & Interceptor Module (Axios)
- Amazon S3 & Amazon CloudFront
- API Gateway / Load Balancer

## Relationships
- Customer, Reviewer, Store Administrator -> Single Page Application (SPA) [HTTPS / JSON]
- Single Page Application (SPA) -> API Gateway / Load Balancer [HTTPS / JSON]
- Amazon CloudFront -> Amazon S3 [Internal AWS Protocol]

## Technology Stack
- React & TypeScript: Type-safe, component-driven UI development
- Redux Toolkit: Predictable state management for complex cart workflows
- Axios: Centralized HTTP client with interceptors for auth and tracing
- Amazon S3 & CloudFront: Static hosting and global edge delivery for <2s performance
- DOMPurify: Client-side sanitization against XSS in user reviews

## Rationale
This architecture ensures high performance, global availability, and strict security compliance while handling 1 million monthly active users. Decoupling the SPA components guarantees maintainability and seamless scalability across regions.

API Gateway / Load Balancer.analysis:
## Overview
The Online Bookstore is a scaled-down Amazon-style e-commerce site designed to provide scalable catalogue browsing, secure checkout, reviews, and personalized book recommendations. The architecture leverages a distributed AWS cloud deployment across three global regions to ensure high availability and performance.

## Key Elements
* Amazon CloudFront (CDN / Edge Router)
* Application Load Balancer (ALB)
* Amazon API Gateway / Authorizer
* AWS ECS Microservices (Catalogue, Checkout, Recommendations, Review Services)
* Amazon Route 53 (Global Traffic Management)
* AWS WAF and AWS Shield (Security & DDoS Mitigation)

## Relationships
* Client / SPA -> Amazon CloudFront: Sends client traffic with injected geo-location headers [HTTPS]
* Amazon CloudFront -> Amazon API Gateway / ALB: Forwards dynamic API calls [HTTPS]
* Amazon API Gateway -> AWS ECS Microservices: Routes validated requests signed with AWS IAM SigV4 [HTTPS / REST]
* Amazon Route 53 -> Amazon CloudFront: Provides latency-based global routing and failover health checks [DNS]

## Technology Stack
* Amazon CloudFront: Handles TLS termination, Geo-DNS routing, and static asset caching at the edge
* Amazon API Gateway & ALB: Manages API routing, JWT validation via cached JWKS, and rate-limiting
* AWS ECS Fargate: Runs containerized microservices without server management overhead
* AWS WAF & AWS Shield: Provides automated OWASP Top-10 mitigations, rate-based rules, and DDoS protection
* Terraform / AWS CDK: Manages infrastructure as code across multi-region deployments

## Rationale
This architecture ensures 99.95% uptime and supports 1 million MAU by decoupling edge routing, security enforcement, and backend microservices across multiple AWS regions. Furthermore, utilizing edge geo-header injection and local token validation maintains low latency and performance under 2 seconds even on constrained networks.

Catalogue & Search Service.analysis:
## Overview
[The Online Bookstore Catalogue & Search Service is a containerized microservice that handles high-performance product discovery, faceted filtering, and keyword search for 1M MAU. It ensures low-latency responses, regional availability, and robust fallback mechanisms across AWS cloud regions.]

## Key Elements
- [Search API Controller (Node.js / Express)]
- [Search Query Engine (Node.js)]
- [Database Fallback Handler (Node.js)]
- [Catalogue Sync Worker (Node.js)]
- [Amazon OpenSearch]
- [Amazon ElastiCache (Redis)]
- [Amazon RDS (PostgreSQL)]
- [Amazon API Gateway / Application Load Balancer]

## Relationships
- [API Gateway -> Search API Controller: Routes search queries via HTTPS / REST]
- [Search API Controller -> Search Query Engine: Delegates query processing via in-memory function call]
- [Search Query Engine -> Amazon OpenSearch: Executes search and aggregations via HTTP / REST with AWS SigV4]
- [Search Query Engine -> Database Fallback Handler: Triggers fallback on circuit breaker trip via internal function call]
- [Database Fallback Handler -> Amazon ElastiCache (Redis): Retrieves cached search payloads via Redis protocol]
- [Catalogue Sync Worker -> Amazon OpenSearch: Synchronizes catalogue index via asynchronous events]

## Technology Stack
- [AWS ECS / Fargate: Serverless container orchestration for scalability and auto-scaling]
- [Amazon OpenSearch: Primary search engine for fast keyword lookup and faceted aggregations]
- [Node.js / Express: Lightweight, high-performance runtime for API controllers and workers]
- [Amazon ElastiCache (Redis): Caching layer for fast fallback responses during outages]
- [AWS IAM & Secrets Manager: Credential-less task authentication and automated secret rotation]

## Rationale
[This architecture decouples search from the primary database using OpenSearch and Redis caching, guaranteeing sub-2-second page loads and high availability. It integrates robust security controls, strict input sanitization, and least-privilege networking to meet compliance, scalability, and uptime goals.]

Checkout & Cart Service.analysis:
## Overview
The Checkout & Cart Service is a secure, highly scalable microservice that manages shopping cart operations, multi-currency pricing, and transactional checkout processing for the Online Bookstore. It ensures reliable, PCI-compliant payment orchestration while supporting the platform's global availability and high-throughput requirements.

## Key Elements
- Cart Management Component (Node.js / Express)
- Checkout Orchestrator Component (Node.js / TypeScript)
- Payment Integration Component (Node.js / TypeScript)
- Order Fulfillment Component (Node.js / TypeScript)
- Currency & Pricing Sub-module
- Amazon ECS / Fargate
- Amazon ElastiCache (Redis)
- Amazon RDS (PostgreSQL)
- Amazon SQS / SNS
- AWS Secrets Manager & AWS WAF

## Relationships
- API Gateway -> Checkout & Cart Service: Routes cart and checkout requests [HTTPS / REST over TLS 1.3]
- Cart Management Component -> Amazon ElastiCache (Redis): Retrieves and persists cart state [Redis Protocol]
- Payment Integration Component -> Payment Gateway: Processes secure payments [HTTPS / REST via Outbox Pattern]
- Order Fulfillment Component -> Shipping Provider APIs & Identity Service: Dispatches orders and events [Amazon SQS / SNS]
- Checkout & Cart Service -> Amazon RDS (PostgreSQL): Reads and writes transactional data and outbox events [PostgreSQL Protocol]

## Technology Stack
- Node.js / TypeScript: Standardized runtime for all internal components, ensuring type safety and shared domain logic.
- Amazon ECS / Fargate: Container orchestration providing elastic scalability without server management.
- Amazon ElastiCache (Redis): Low-latency in-memory data store for ephemeral cart management and session persistence.
- Amazon RDS (PostgreSQL): Relational database utilizing the Outbox Pattern for reliable transactional processing.
- AWS Secrets Manager: Secure credential storage enforcing automated 30-day rotation for API keys.
- AWS App Mesh / WAF: Enforces internal mTLS traffic boundaries and protects endpoints against card-testing attacks.

## Rationale
This architecture guarantees 99.95% availability and high scalability to handle 1 million MAU through decoupled, elastic container components deployed on AWS. The Outbox Pattern and strict single-region write model protect financial data integrity while meeting rigorous GDPR, CCPA, and PCI-DSS compliance standards.

Recommendation Service.analysis:
## Overview
[The Online Bookstore system provides a scalable e-commerce platform for purchasing books with integrated recommendations and reviews. The Recommendation Service delivers personalized and curated book suggestions to maximize user engagement and average order value.]

## Key Elements
[
- Shoppers and Store Administrators
- Recommendation API Container (Node.js / Express)
- Background Worker Container (Python / FastAPI)
- Amazon ElastiCache (Redis)
- Amazon Kinesis
- Amazon RDS (PostgreSQL)
]

## Relationships
[
- API Gateway to Recommendation API: Fetches recommendations [HTTPS / REST]
- Recommendation API to Amazon ElastiCache (Redis): Reads pre-computed or fallback lists [Redis protocol, <50ms]
- Background Worker to Amazon Kinesis: Consumes clickstream events [TCP]
- Background Worker to Amazon RDS (PostgreSQL): Manages promotional rules and audit logs [TCP / SQL]
- Background Worker to Amazon ElastiCache (Redis): Writes merged recommendation payloads [Redis protocol]
]

## Technology Stack
[
- Node.js / Express: Powers the lightweight Recommendation API for high-throughput reads.
- Python / FastAPI: Implements the background worker for scoring, ranking, and merchandising logic.
- Amazon ElastiCache (Redis): Provides sub-50ms cache lookups and multi-region Global Datastores.
- Amazon Kinesis: Ingests real-time shopper clickstream events.
- Amazon RDS (PostgreSQL): Stores promotional overrides and audit logs securely.
]

## Rationale
[Asynchronous pre-computation of recommendations directly to Redis eliminates compute dependencies on the critical request path, guaranteeing sub-50ms lookups. Regional isolation via ElastiCache Global Datastores and in-memory fallbacks ensure high availability and strict adherence to performance NFRs.]

Review Service.analysis:
## Overview
The Online Bookstore is a globally scaled e-commerce system providing physical and electronic book purchasing, catalog browsing, and personalized recommendations. The architecture leverages AWS multi-region infrastructure to ensure high availability, performance, and GDPR compliance.

## Key Elements
- Customers (Shoppers, Registered Reviewers, Content Moderators)
- Amazon API Gateway / Application Load Balancer
- Single Page Application (React / TypeScript, Amazon S3, Amazon CloudFront)
- Review Service (AWS ECS / Fargate, Spring Boot / Java)
- Catalogue & Search, Checkout & Cart, and Recommendation Services
- Amazon RDS (PostgreSQL with read replicas) and Amazon ElastiCache (Redis)
- Amazon SQS, SNS, and Kinesis

## Relationships
- Customer -> Single Page Application [HTTPS]
- Single Page Application -> API Gateway / Load Balancer [HTTPS / REST]
- API Gateway -> Review Service API Controller [HTTPS / REST]
- Review Service -> Amazon SQS / SNS [AWS SQS/SNS protocol]
- Review Service -> Amazon RDS (PostgreSQL) [JDBC / PostgreSQL]
- Review Service -> Identity & Notification Service [HTTPS / REST]

## Technology Stack
- **Frontend:** React / TypeScript hosted on Amazon S3 and distributed via Amazon CloudFront for sub-2-second page loads.
- **Compute:** AWS ECS / Fargate containers managed via Terraform and automated CI/CD pipelines.
- **Database:** Amazon RDS (PostgreSQL) with cross-region read replicas for multi-region scalability.
- **Messaging:** Amazon SQS and SNS for decoupled, asynchronous event-driven processing and high availability.
- **Security:** AWS KMS for data encryption at rest, TLS 1.3 for transit, and JSON Web Tokens (JWT) for RBAC.

## Rationale
This architecture decouples core domains using asynchronous messaging via SQS/SNS to guarantee 99.95% availability and resilience against traffic spikes. Utilizing ECS Fargate, multi-region RDS replicas, and AWS edge services satisfies stringent performance, security, and global scaling requirements.

Database.analysis:
## Overview
The Online Bookstore system uses a regionally partitioned PostgreSQL database architecture on AWS to ensure GDPR/CCPA compliance and low-latency transactions. It securely manages user data, multi-currency catalogs, and asynchronous event streaming for recommendations.

## Key Elements
- Core Transaction Engine (Amazon RDS PostgreSQL)
- Catalog & JSONB Store
- CDC Publisher (AWS DMS / Debezium)
- Amazon Kinesis
- AWS Secrets Manager
- Amazon CloudWatch

## Relationships
- Checkout & Cart Service -> Core Transaction Engine: Executes ACID writes [PostgreSQL protocol, TLS 1.3, IAM Auth]
- Catalogue & Search Service -> Catalog & JSONB Store: Queries product details [PostgreSQL protocol, TLS 1.3]
- Database -> Amazon Kinesis: Streams transaction events for recommendations [CDC / PostgreSQL Logical Decoding]
- Database -> Amazon CloudWatch: Routes audit logs and performance metrics [AWS API]

## Technology Stack
- Amazon RDS (PostgreSQL with read replicas): Provides ACID compliance and Multi-AZ high availability.
- JSONB: Enables flexible product metadata storage.
- AWS DMS / Debezium: Facilitates low-latency change data capture (CDC).
- AWS Secrets Manager: Secures credentials with automatic rotation.

## Rationale
Regionally isolated database instances enforce strict GDPR/CCPA data residency requirements across all deployment regions. Asynchronous CDC streaming via Kinesis protects checkout performance while feeding recommendations.
